references.text: The psalm describes God as 'he who rides on the clouds', using the same imagery found in Deuteronomy where God 'rides on the heavens'
God is described as the one who 'rides over the ancient skies', parallel to the image of God riding through the sky to help his people
God is described as the one who 'rode upon a cherub and flew, he soared on the wings of the wind', a similar picture of God's majestic journey through the heavens
The Lord 'rides on a light cloud', using the same theophanic imagery that shows God's sovereignty over the sky
'Who is like you among the gods, O Lord?' - the same confession that no one is like God, similar to the opening statement 'There is none like God'
'There is none like you among the gods, O Lord' - a direct parallel to the confession that no one is like the God of Israel
'I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like me' - affirming the uniqueness of the God of Israel
God is described as the one who comes with horses and chariots for salvation, resembling the image of God riding to help his people
